answer: Topological Cut-Point Scoring. For each new agent, measure the delta between its neighborhood overlap with existing agents and the baseline expected from random attachment; identities created in one burst share neighbors and produce near-zero overlap delta. Enforce admission only when an identity connects through distinct, previously unlinked regions of the graph. An attacker must rent or build separate copper-grade hosting paths and sustain comet-like bursts of unrelated links to fake that spread, paying for genuinely disjoint network placement per identity rather than cheap duplicates.
